insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in extract (Base Sum Insured + Booster+ SI + Safeguard/Safeguard+ SI + ReAssure+/ReAssureX as per Policy Schedule/variant)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: “We don’t limit your choice. Choose the room you like, but choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: No room rent cap is mentioned, so you can choose any room category. Higher room costs can still consume your Sum Insured faster, reducing what remains for other hospital bills.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “ReAssure “Forever”: Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure “Forever”. Once Triggered it stays for life, provided that the policy is renewed without break.”
great.explanation: After the first paid claim, an unlimited additional Sum Insured feature gets triggered and then continues for life if you renew without a break. This can protect you from multiple large hospitalizations over the long term.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured... (this 10 Lakh will trigger unlimited times)”
great.explanation: Sum Insured can be restored and triggered unlimited times after it gets used, as shown in the illustration. This reduces the risk of running out of cover after one or more claims in the same policy period.

great.name: PED Waiting Period
great.quote: “Pre-existing Diseases... shall be excluded until the expiry of 12months/24 months/ 36 months (as per Variant selected) of continuous coverage”
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 12/24/36 months depending on the variant selected. If you choose the 12-month variant, it is faster than the common 24–48 months in the market.

great.name: Specific Illness Waiting
great.quote: “Specified disease/procedure... excluded until the expiry of 24 months/12 months (as per Variant Selected)”
great.reference: Section 5.1.2 Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code- Excl02)
great.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are covered after 12 or 24 months depending on the variant selected. The 12-month option gives earlier access than the standard 24-month wait.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident”
good.explanation: Illness treatment is not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will pay expenses... for 60 days before the date of admission”
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses related to a covered hospitalization are payable for up to 60 days before admission. This helps cover tests, consultations, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses related to a covered hospitalization are payable for up to 180 days after discharge. This supports follow-up care like medicines, diagnostics, and consultations.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “Home Care Treatment means treatment availed by the insured person at home... would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken at home...”
good.explanation: Home care/domiciliary treatment is covered when the condition would otherwise require hospital care but is taken at home. This can be useful when hospitalization is not feasible or medically advised against.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “Air Ambulance: Only in case of Emergency. We will pay up to Base Sum Insured.”
good.reference: Section 4.1.1(a)-(b) Expenses in reaching a Hospital
good.explanation: Emergency air ambulance is covered up to the Base Sum Insured. This can help in critical situations where rapid transport is needed, though it can be expensive.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments, up to Base Sum Insured for the list as specified below...”
good.explanation: Modern treatments are covered up to the Base Sum Insured, but only for the listed procedures. Coverage is therefore available but not open-ended for all new-age treatments.

good.name: Cashless Network
good.quote: “Cashless claim facility is available at our network hospitals ONLY... for the latest list, refer to our website www.nivabupa.com.”
good.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at the insurer’s network hospitals, with the current list hosted on the website. You should verify whether your preferred hospitals are in-network before relying on cashless.

bad.name: Co-pay (Optional)
bad.quote: “Borderless... Choose from a range of co-payments options 0%, 20%, 30%, 40% & 50%”
bad.explanation: Worldwide cover (Borderless) is offered with selectable co-pay options of 0%, 20%, 30%, 40% or 50%. Any co-pay means you may have to pay that percentage of every admissible claim under this option.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “The expenses that are not covered... Annexure I - The expenses that are not covered...”
bad.reference: Section 6.2.4(c) and Annexure I; plus Safeguard description in 4.1.20/4.1.21
bad.explanation: Non-payable items/consumables listed in Annexure I are excluded by default. This can increase out-of-pocket costs unless you buy an optional safeguard that covers such items.

bad.name: NCB
bad.quote: Not mentioned in the provided policy wording extract.
bad.explanation: No No Claim Bonus/renewal bonus is stated in the provided extract. If the policy truly has no NCB, your Sum Insured may not grow for claim-free years.

unclear.name: Restore Benefit Variant
unclear.quote: “Either ReAssure+ or ReAssureX can be offered in a single policy.”
unclear.explanation: Only one restore variant (ReAssure+ or ReAssureX) applies to a policy at a time. You need to check your policy schedule to know which rules and triggers apply to your cover.

unclear.name: Room Type Modification
unclear.quote: “Room Type Modification... You can choose between a Standard Single Room and a Shared Room up to Sum Insured... You will have to bear additional co-payment IF treatment is taken in a higher room category than the eligible room category”
unclear.explanation: If this optional modification is chosen, your eligible room category becomes restricted (Standard Single Room or Shared Room). Taking treatment in a higher room category can trigger an additional co-payment, increasing your out-of-pocket share.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
